summary: UCSB describes new console attachments for its IBM 360/75 through an interface called the MLC/360M, which gives 32 independently addressed I/O connections in 16 pairs for devices over RS-232 style signals. It explains the first group of attachments.

eli5.summary: A university adds extra sockets to its big computer so more kinds of terminals can plug in.

subtitle: Adding I/O ports to UCSB's IBM 360/75 computer for multiple terminals

tldr.problem: UCSB's IBM 360/75 computer had limited I/O connections and needed to support many different kinds of terminals and devices.
tldr.mechanism: UCSB designed the MLC/360M (Multi-Line Controller/360M), an interface unit that provides 32 independently addressed I/O connections in 16 pairs, using standard EIA RS-232 signal levels for compatibility with modems and terminals.
tldr.outcome: The system proved flexible enough to support everything from 300 baud acoustic couplers to 9600 baud classroom use, including Tektronix display terminals and specialized graphics equipment.

today: RFC 311 documents UCSB's infrastructure expansion in 1972. The MLC/360M represents an early example of standardized I/O interfaces for connecting diverse terminals to a mainframe computer.

sections.title: The MLC/360M Interface
sections.content: UCSB's IBM 360/75 computer needed a way to connect many different I/O devices. The Multi-Line Controller/360M (MLC/360M) is an interface unit attached to the computer's Multiplexor Channel that provides 32 independently addressed I/O connections grouped into 16 pairs for full-duplex communication. Each input group has a 16-bit buffer and each output group has a 32-bit buffer.
sections.eli5: The MLC/360M gives the computer 16 pairs of plugs, so 16 devices can talk to it at the same time.

sections.title: Standard Signals for Easy Compatibility
sections.content: The interface uses EIA RS-232 signal levels, the standard for data communication equipment of the era. This allowed attachment of common devices like 201B data-sets at 2400 baud. The hardware and software are designed to be easily modified for new device types, making it adaptable to a wide range of uses.
sections.eli5: The system uses a standard plug type, so many different devices can work with it.

sections.title: Support for Many Terminal Types
sections.content: The MLC/360M proved flexible in practice. In addition to the standard Culler-Fried graphic display consoles used in educational classrooms, UCSB successfully attached a Tektronix 4002A terminal capable of upper and lower case ASCII, and the NIH General Purpose Graphics Terminal (GPGT), a delay-line refreshed video display with graphics capability developed at the University of Iowa for biomedical applications. The system has been used at speeds from 300 baud acoustic couplers to 9600 baud for multi-station classroom operation.
sections.eli5: Many different kinds of displays and terminals worked with it, from slow acoustic couplers to fast classroom terminals.
